payload.claim: The breaker is only evaluated before starting the next candidate (line 113), while the counter itself is updated after each candidate returns (lines 136-143). If the two (or more) candidates that trigger the threshold are the last ones in `candidates`, the loop exits normally at line 145 and closes the batch as `DRAINED` instead of `INFRASTRUCTURE`, even though the standing abort count reached the threshold. This silently misreports why the night ended in the one column (`batches.status`) the design says exists precisely to distinguish 'the toolchain is broken' from an ordinary drain — no test exercises a queue whose trailing candidates are the ones that trip the breaker.
